title: Read a Grid in a Spiral
statement:
You get a grid grid with m rows and n columns. Read every value exactly once by walking a clockwise spiral: start at the top-left cell, go right along the top row, then down the right edge, left along the bottom row, up the left edge, and keep circling inward until every cell has been visited.

Return the values in the order you visit them. The grid does not have to be square.

examples.why: After the outer ring, only the middle row piece 6, 7 is left, read left to right. Going round again after 6, 7 would read 6 a second time.
One column. The top row is just 3, the right edge is 8, 1, and there is no bottom row or left edge left to walk back up, so nothing repeats.
A tall grid: after the ring the inside is empty. A walker that only checks the row bounds would read 6 or 8 twice.

hints: Keep four walls: the first and last row not yet read, and the first and last column not yet read.
One lap reads the top row, the right column, the bottom row, then the left column, and each side pulls its wall one step inward.
After the top row and right column, check that a bottom row and a left column still exist before reading them. That check is what stops a single leftover row or column from being read twice.

explain.intuition:
Picture four walls closing in: top, bottom, left, right. Reading the top row uses it up, so top moves down one. Reading the right column moves right left one, and so on. The spiral is just those four sides in turn, until the walls cross.

The only subtle part is a grid that is not square. After a few laps, what is left might be a single row or a single column. You read it once going right (or down). If you then blindly read "the bottom row going left", you would read the same row again backwards. So before the bottom and left sides, check that top ≤ bottom and left ≤ right still hold.
steps: While top ≤ bottom and left ≤ right: read row top from left to right, then top++.
If top ≤ bottom, read row bottom from right down to left, then bottom−−.
If left ≤ right, read column left from bottom up to top, then left++.
pitfalls: Skipping the two checks in the middle of a lap. A 3 × 2 or 1 × 4 grid then reads some values twice.
Looping until the output has m × n values but not stopping mid-lap. The last lap can overshoot and push extra values past the count.
Mixing up rows and columns: grid[r][c] is row first. With a non-square grid the swap throws or reads undefined.

solutions.title: Walk and turn when blocked
solutions.idea: Simulate a walker that moves right, down, left, up in turn. It turns whenever the next cell is outside the grid or already visited.
solutions.py:
class Solution:
    def spiralRead(self, grid: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        seen = [[False] * n for _ in range(m)]
        moves = [(0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1), (-1, 0)]
        out, r, c, d = [], 0, 0, 0
        for _ in range(m * n):
            out.append(grid[r][c])
            seen[r][c] = True
            nr, nc = r + moves[d][0], c + moves[d][1]
            if not (0 <= nr < m and 0 <= nc < n) or seen[nr][nc]:
                d = (d + 1) % 4
            r, c = r + moves[d][0], c + moves[d][1]
        return out

solutions.title: Four shrinking walls
solutions.idea: Read the top row, right column, bottom row and left column, moving each wall inward after reading it. Check that walls have not crossed before the bottom and left sides.

followups: Do the reverse: given m, n and a list of values, fill a grid in spiral order.
Walk counter-clockwise, starting down the left edge. What changes?
Return only the k-th value of the spiral without building the whole list. Can you skip whole rings?
